Closed 2026-07-27: Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions' TWO complete passes are modelled. `Relic` declares `modify_card_reward_options` (the plain pass) and `modify_card_reward_options_late` as SEPARATE members (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:305-325), and rewards.create_reward_cards runs every relic's plain hook and THEN every relic's Late hook (sts2_rl/rewards.py:460-476), which is Hook.cs:1444-1466. A Late implementer is therefore guaranteed to see everything the plain pass added, whatever order the relics were picked up in. Frozen Egg is a Late implementer (sts2_rl/relics/_eggs.py:46-53 `modify_card_reward_options_late`); the effect itself already matched EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards.

ModifyMerchantCardCreationResults.rationale: FrozenEgg.cs:35-41 delegates to the same EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards with the same card type and no flags check, and _eggs.py:44-45 delegates to the same `modify_card_reward_options` body. The owner guard is N1 (waived). MerchantCardEntry computes the price from the modified card on both sides because the hook runs before pricing (relics/base.py:333-336 says so).

TryModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck.rationale: FrozenEgg.cs:43-61 checks owner, `card.Type != CardType.Power`, `!card.IsUpgradable`, then CloneCards the card, upgrades the CLONE and returns it as `newCard`; _eggs.py:47-51 checks the same two card conditions through `_applies` and upgrades the card IN PLACE, returning the same object. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): an Inflame added to the deck comes out at upgrade_level 1 and is the same object that was passed in. Verdicted a divergence rather than a gap under binding rule 2 because the observable -- the deck's (id, upgrade_level) contents, which conformance/runner.py compares -- is identical, and a freshly created card entering the deck carries no per-instance state for CloneCard to preserve. It is NOT waived and NOT faithful: the identity difference is real, and see guard G3 for the one shape where it would matter.

guards.what: G2: `options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoHookUpgrades) -> return false` (FrozenEgg.cs:27-30) has no sim counterpart
guards.rationale: MECHANISM NoHookUpgrades, one verdict at all THREE egg sites (relic/toxic_egg N1, relic/frozen_egg G2, relic/molten_egg G3) after the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass reconciled them -- they previously split two waivers against one gap on identical facts, which binding rule 3 forbids. VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE the member is dead, and the grep is EXECUTED and exhaustive: `grep -rn NoHookUpgrades src/` returns exactly FOUR lines in the whole game source -- the enum member `NoHookUpgrades = 4` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs:29) and the three egg relics READING it (FrozenEgg.cs:27, MoltenEgg.cs:27, ToxicEgg.cs:27). THREE READERS, ZERO PRODUCERS. The two composite flags that could set it indirectly are dead too: `grep -rn 'CardCreationFlags.NoUpgrades\b' src/` returns NOTHING, and `grep -rn NoModifications src/` returns only its own declaration (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs:68). `CardCreationOptions.Flags` has a private setter and is writable only through `WithFlags` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationOptions.cs:57, 211-215), and all 29 `WithFlags` call sites were enumerated (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-molten`) with the same result. So the guard can never be true for any card creation the shipping game performs. THIS ALSO RETRACTS relic/frozen_egg G2's stated dormancy trigger, which was 'porting any C# effect that creates cards WithFlags(NoHookUpgrades) -- the shape exists in the source's card-generation callers'. IT DOES NOT: no such caller exists anywhere under src/, so there is no unported content that would make this live, which is exactly what distinguishes a dead member from a dormant gap. The genuinely live sibling flag is `NoModifyHooks`, which HAS a real producer -- LastingCandy.cs:127 builds `WithFlags(CardCreationFlags.NoModifyHooks | CardCreationFlags.NoCardPoolModifications)` and CardFactory.cs:104 gates the whole `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` dispatch on it. That is a live C# path with no sim counterpart and it belongs to relic/lasting_candy's record, not to the eggs. Rule 7: src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs, src/Core/Runs/CardCreationOptions.cs, src/Core/Factories/CardFactory.cs and src/Core/Models/Relics/LastingCandy.cs are cited and not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3: the sim upgrades the ORIGINAL card object where C# substitutes an upgraded CloneCard (FrozenEgg.cs:58-59; EggRelicHelper.cs:17-19)
guards.issue: PROMPT.md bug class 17 at the egg relics' two sites. CardScope.CloneCard -> ClonePreservingMutability (CardModel.cs:2168-2179) carries upgrade level, enchantment, affliction, keyword edits and local energy-cost modifiers; the sim has no clone helper at all (sweep E). Same mechanism, same verdict as audit/records/relic/burning_sticks.json G3 -- binding rule 3. DORMANT here, and for a reason worth stating precisely: because the sim MUTATES rather than rebuilds, it does not lose per-instance state the way sweep E's five rebuild sites do -- the divergence is the reverse, that the game keeps the un-upgraded ORIGINAL alive and adds a new model. That matters only where something holds a reference to the pre-modification card: `CardCreationResult.ModifyCard(newCard, source)` records the original for the reward screen's 'modified by' display (presentation), and a merchant entry re-reads its card. The concrete thing that would make it live is a sim effect that keeps a handle on a card across add_card -- e.g. a relic reacting to after_card_added_to_deck and comparing identity with the offered option. _eggs.py:19 states the in-place choice deliberately, which is why this is filed as the class-17 gap rather than as a port error.
